Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 25-Nov-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Data Structures [ECM_2125]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                    Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Write a function Reverse to reverse the elements of an integer array using pointer. Access the         (4)  
  elements of the array using dereference operator. Read the values from the keyboard in main  
  A)           function. Display the result in the main function.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Define integer pointer, character pointer and float pointer with examples. Write a short program to    (3)  
  swap two integers using pass by reference method.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)           Determine and explain the functionality of the following code fragment and write the output of any     (3)  
  sample input.  
  void Funtion1(int a[], int n)  
  {  
  $$for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; i += 2)$$  
  {  
  $$int temp = a[i];$$  
  $$a[i] = a[i + 1];$$  
  $$a[i + 1] = temp;$$  
  }  
  }  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                You are given the following sequence of letters and asterisks:                                         (4)  
  EAS*Y*QUE***ST***IO*N***  
  A)           Each letter (such as E) represents an insert operation of that element into a data structure, and  
  each asterisk (*) represents a remove operation.  
  
  1. Assume the data structure is a Stack (LIFO order). Show the sequence of elements that  
  would be removed (output sequence) during the remove operations.  
  2. Assume the data structure is a Queue (FIFO order). Show the sequence of elements that  
  would be removed (output sequence) during the remove operations.  
  3. Compare and explain briefly how and why the two output sequences differ, even though  
  the same sequence of operations is applied.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  Page #1

B)   Write a C program that accepts integers continuously and inserts them into a stack until the user           (3)  
  enters a negative number. Display all elements in the stack.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Convert the given infix expression to prefix expression. Show the content of Stack at every step:           (3)  
  A + B * (C ^ D - E) ^ (F + G * H) - I  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)        Write the structure definition for a singly linked list node in C and function definitions to perform the   (4)  
  following operations:  
  A)   i) Insert a new node at the end of the list  
  ii) Display the data of the middle node by traversing the list only once  
  iii) Display all node data in reverse order without actually reversing the list  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)   Write a C Program to do the following:                                                                      (3)  
  i) Create a circular singly linked list where each node contains an integer value.  
  ii) Insert a new node with a specified value after every node containing an even integer.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)   write a c program to implement stack using linked list and implement push() and pop() operation             (3)  
  with all necessary conditions  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)        Consider a following sequence 40, 20, 60, 10, 30, 50, 70, Construct a binary search tree (BST) by           (4)  
  inserting the elements in the order given above. Draw the resulting BST.  
  A)  
  1. Write a C program to insert a new integer element into the BST while maintaining the BST  
  property. The program should:  
  
  Take the new element as input from the user  
  Insert the element in the correct position in the BST  
  Display the BST using inorder traversal after insertion  
  
  Write a recursive C function to search for a given integer element in the BST. The function should  
  return whether the element is present or not.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)   A circular queue of size 6 is initially empty. Perform the following operations: ENQUEUE(10),               (3)  
  ENQUEUE(20), ENQUEUE(30), ENQUEUE(40), DEQUEUE(), ENQUEUE(50), ENQUEUE(60),  
  ENQUEUE(70), DEQUEUE(), ENQUEUE(80)  
  
  i) Show the contents of the queue after each operation.  
  ii) Track Front (F) and Rear (R) pointers after every step.  
  iii) Identify the step where overflow occurs and justify your answer.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)   Given three sequences:                                                                                      (3)  
  (i) 28, 16, 11, 19, 17, 25  
  (ii) 11, 16, 17, 19, 25, 28  
  (iii) 11, 17, 25, 19, 16, 28  
  Determine which one is preorder, inorder, and postorder sequences of the same binary tree, and  
  construct that tree.  
  
  
  Page #2

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
5)                       Write a BFS Traversal sequence of the following Graph. Write the function to find the BFS taking as (4)  
  the parameter the value of the vertex from which BFS (depth first search) has to be carried out.  
  A)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)               Define the following for the binary tree.                                                                (3)  
  
  1. What is n-ary tree.  
  2. Strict n-ary tree.  
  3. Height Vs. Node  
  4. Internal Vs. External Node  
  
  Indegree Vs Outdegree  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)               Construct a binary tree given its inorder and preorder sequence as B F G H P R S T W Y Z and P F (3)  
  B H G S R Y T W Z respectively. Also write the postorder traversal sequence for the constructed  
  binary tree.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
